subject: How to help users with install issues?

messages.author: 6a3b777d6a18967b
messages.subject: How to help users with install issues?
parts:
A few weeks ago I was thrilled to be able to share my R package with people via github thru the help of devtools.  Now I am in a new position: some people cannot run my examples, and I am not sure how to help them.  For reference:

Here is my project: https://github.com/trulia/choroplethr
Here is my forum for people to report problems: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/choroplethr

The first two issues were resolved by asking people to upgrade their version of R from 2.15 to 3.0.2.  However, now someone has reported an issue with 3.0.2:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/choroplethr/ixFezN2EG8U

I began following up by asking him to clarify what OS he is using since I didn't immediately recognize it.  Once I have that I am planning to try to get a machine with that OS that I can then try to debug locally.

I'm wondering though: is there a standard list of Q&A that people normally run thru when they try to help people remotely with their packages?  I'm basically just making this up as I go along, and was wondering if there is a better way.

Thanks.

Ari

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: How to help users with install issues?
parts:
The best way in general is to get your package on cran. This is painful, obviously, but does avoid many potential installation problems. 

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: How to help users with install issues?

On 2 Feb 2014, at 21:54, Hadley Wickham wrote:

The best way in general is to get your package on cran. This is painful, obviously, but does avoid many potential installation problems.

Are you already using devtools::build_win()? This is the best way that I know of short of CRAN to exercise your examples and tests. It is essential before a CRAN release, but is also pretty useful for any github milestone.

Best,

Greg.
